**Note to Users**: The primary requirement to run the main Blue Water Potential Toolkit (`02_Blue-Water.qmd`) is the set of standardized static CSV inputs, combined with the dynamic phenology curves generated by this script. 

### 🗂️ Overview & Data Summary

This script processes, visualizes, and expands eight distinct categories of input data required by the hydrological model:

1. **Climatic Forcings**: Multi-year Daily Precipitation and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0).
2. **Soil Properties**: Water Holding Capacity (WHC) and Readily Available Water (RAW).
3. **Crop Parameters**: Rooting depths and whether the crop is irrigated or rainfed.
4. **Crop Cycle**: Sowing date, phenological phase duration, and crop coefficients (Kc) according to the FAO-56 method (Allen et al., 1998).
5. **Cropping Systems**: Crop rotation at the plot scale.
6. **Farm Production Systems**: Aggregation of grazed and cropped area (ha) for each farming system.
7. **Agrarian System**: Area (ha) of each farm production system in a given village/micro-region.
8. **Model Parameters**: The master configuration file. This defines global baseline assumptions, including seasonal bare-soil evaporation coefficients (kc_dry_season, kc_kharip), the calendar day to switch between them (doy_switch), the starting soil moisture fraction (sm_init), and the soil_input routing switch—which dictates whether the model should use raw Precipitation (P) or calculate surface runoff to use Effective Precipitation (Peff).

*In Hemingway et al. (202X), this process was run for two agrarian systems, corresponding to two historical periods: the 1950s and 2022. The climate time series (1980-2018) was held constant to isolate the impact of land-use changes, while cropping systems, production systems, and agrarian systems were period-specific.*

---

### 🗂️ Data Architecture & Workflow

The Blue Water Potential Toolkit uses a strict, automated pipeline to separate user-provided data from model-generated data. 

**1. `data/input/` (The User Interface)**
This folder is the starting point of the toolkit. It holds all the static, standardized CSV files listed above. **If you are adapting this toolkit for your own study site, this is the only folder you need to populate.**

**2. `data/processed/` (The Phenology Module)**
This folder is fully automated. When you render this script (`01_Prepare_Model_Input.qmd`), it reads the static parameters from `data/input/`, executes the mathematical rule-sets (FAO-56 segments, polynomial equations, grazing regrowth), and outputs the continuous daily Crop Coefficient ($K_c$) tables here. *Users do not need to manually edit files in this folder.*

---

### 📂 Directory Structure for this Script

The Blue Water Potential Toolkit serves two purposes: it can be used to reproduce the results presented in Hemingway et al. (202X), and it can be applied to new study sites. As the first step in the pipeline, this script is where both workflows begin.

* **Reproducing the Manuscript:** All clean inputs required to run this script are already provided in the `data/input/` directory.
* **Adapting for your own study site:** Place your clean data in the `data/input/` folder. The script will automatically generate the required folder structure for all derived processed outputs. To run this script, open the `.Rproj` and click "Render".

```text
project_root/
├── data/
│   ├── input/                       <- REQUIRED: Drop your 10 standardized CSVs here
│   │   ├── 01_model_parameters.csv
│   │   ├── 02_precipitation.csv
│   │   ├── 03_et0.csv
│   │   ├── 04_soil.parameters.csv
│   │   ├── 05_crop.parameters.csv
│   │   ├── 06_fao_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv
│   │   ├── 07_step_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv (optional)
│   │   ├── 08_crop.systems.csv
│   │   ├── 09_crop_system_area_by_production_system.csv
│   │   └── 10_no_of_farmers_by_production_system.csv
│   └── processed/                   <- AUTOMATED: Derived model requirements land here
│       └── supplementary/           <- Generated: Intermediary Kc tables
├── code/
│   ├── functions/                   <- Core toolkit mathematical dependencies
│   ├── 01_Prepare_Model_Inputs.qmd  <- (This file)
│   └── 01_Prepare_Model_Inputs.html <- Generated: HTML Report created by rendering this script
└── Blue-Water.Rproj                 <- Required: RStudio Project file to render this script
```

# Append expected data types for the end-user display

  dplyr::mutate(
    description = dplyr::case_when(
      parameter == "soil_input" ~ base::paste0(description, "<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Expected: Character string ('P' or 'Peff')</small>"),
      TRUE ~ base::paste0(description, "<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Expected: Numeric</small>")

# Climatic Data (Forcing Variables)

The water balance model requires continuous, daily forcing variables. Here, we read the required daily Precipitation (P) and Reference Evapotranspiration (ET0).

```{r clim-load}
precip <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/02_precipitation.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
et0.daily <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/03_et0.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
et0.daily <- et0.daily %>%
  dplyr::mutate(et0 = base::round(et0, 3))

base::stopifnot(
  "Error: Precipitation contains missing values (NA)." = !base::any(base::is.na(precip$p)),
  "Error: ET0 contains missing values (NA)." = !base::any(base::is.na(et0.daily$et0))
)
# Only for figure plotting
climate_summary <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/supplementary/01_monthly_climatology_for_figure.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
```

## Crop Coefficient (Kc) Curves

Our framework dynamically generates daily Kc curves over a calendar year from the input parameters. As described in the manuscript, daily Kc values are computed based on the FAO method for most crops, monthly step functions for some fruit trees, or polynomial equations for groundnut, or linear regrowth rules for grasslands. Some crops such as banana can span multiple years, in which case we define a crop coefficient curve of each year independently.

```{r load-kc-params}
fao_kc_raw       <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/06_fao_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
fruit_kc_raw   <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/07_step_kc_curve_parameters_table.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
```

#### FAO Segmented Parameters

---

We pass the input Kc parameters through mathematical functions. This includes standard FAO-56 segmented curves for standard crops, derived 4th-order polynomial equations for continuous rapid growth crops like Groundnuts, and complex daily linear regrowth rates for pastures and harvested grasses.

### Standard FAO-56 Segmented Curves

Generates the classic 4-stage linear growth curves for standard crops.

```{r generate-fao-kc, warning=FALSE, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 10, fig.cap="Standard FAO-56 segmented curves based on major crop calendar events such as sowing and harvesting dates, and crop development duration."}
fao_kc_raw.long <- fao_kc_raw %>% 
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = -1, names_to = "crop") %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(crop = stringr::str_to_title(base::gsub("_|\\.", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))

kc <- fao_kc_raw.long %>% 
  base::subset(stringr::str_detect(var, stringr::regex("kc", ignore_case = TRUE))) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(Kc = value, kc_var = var) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(Kc_var = dplyr::case_when(
    base::grepl("ini", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_ini", 
    base::grepl("mid", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_mid", 
    base::grepl("end", kc_var, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Kc_end", 
    TRUE ~ kc_var
  ))

doy <- fao_kc_raw.long %>% 
  base::subset(var %in% c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest")) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(doy = value, doy_var = var) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(doy = dplyr::if_else(doy == 365.00, 366.00, doy))

kc.doy.key <- base::data.frame(doy_var = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"), kc_var = c("Kc_ini", "Kc_ini", "Kc_mid", "Kc_mid", "Kc_end"))

doy <- dplyr::left_join(doy, kc.doy.key, by = c("doy_var"))
kc.doy <- dplyr::left_join(doy, kc, by = c("kc_var", "crop")) %>% 
  dplyr::arrange(crop, doy, Kc) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(doy = base::as.numeric(doy), Kc = base::as.numeric(Kc))

kc.doy.crops <- kc.doy %>% 
  dplyr::select(crop, doy_var, doy, Kc) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(doy_var = base::factor(doy_var, levels = c("Sowing", "End of ini", "End of Dev", "End of Mid", "Harvest"))) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(crop, doy, doy_var)

kc_wide_build <- kc.doy.crops %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = doy_var, values_from = c(doy, Kc)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    Sow = doy_Sowing, E_ini = `doy_End of ini`, E_dev = `doy_End of Dev`,
    E_mid = `doy_End of Mid`, Harv = doy_Harvest,
    K_ini = Kc_Sowing, K_mid = `Kc_End of Dev`, K_end = Kc_Harvest
  )

kc_segmented_ls <- base::lapply(1:base::nrow(kc_wide_build), function(i) build_fao_curve(kc_wide_build[i, ]))
kc_segmented <- dplyr::bind_rows(kc_segmented_ls) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(crop = stringr::str_to_title(base::gsub("_", " ", crop, perl = TRUE)))

# Visual Check
ggplot2::ggplot(
  kc_segmented %>% 
    # 1. Remove the baseline fallow periods entirely
    dplyr::filter(kc > 0) %>% 
    dplyr::arrange(crop, doy) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(crop) %>%
    # 2. Flag contiguous growth phases whenever there is a jump in DOY
    dplyr::mutate(
      is_gap = doy - dplyr::lag(doy, default = dplyr::first(doy)) > 1,
      plot_group = base::paste(crop, base::cumsum(is_gap), sep = "_")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup(), 
  
  # 3. Apply the dynamic group aesthetic!
  ggplot2::aes(x = doy, y = kc, color = crop, group = plot_group)
) +
  ggplot2::geom_area(ggplot2::aes(fill = crop), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) + 
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ crop) + 
  theme_baseR +
  ggplot2::labs(title = "Standard FAO-56 Curves", x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = base::seq(0, 366, 100), limits = c(0, 366)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = base::seq(0, 1.2, 0.3), limits = c(0, 1.2)) +
  ggplot2::theme(legend.position = "none")
```

### Polynomial Curves

Applies 4th-order polynomial equations to capture continuous rapid growth dynamics (e.g., Groundnuts).

```{r generate-poly-kc, warning=FALSE, out.width="70%", fig.cap="Continuous polynomial curves modeling the rapid growth dynamics of groundnuts."}
poly_list <- base::list()

# Only generate the curve if the user included this crop in their data!
if ("Groundnut Summer" %in% crop.param$crop) {
  poly_list[[1]] <- base::data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(crop = "Groundnut Summer", d = doy - 10, 
           kc = dplyr::if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 1.25*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.82*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.8*10^(-3)*d^2 - 2.49*10^(-2)*d + 0.3792, 0))
}

if ("Groundnut Monsoon" %in% crop.param$crop) {
  poly_list[[2]] <- base::data.frame(doy = 1:366) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(crop = "Groundnut Monsoon", d = doy - 182, 
           kc = dplyr::if_else(d >= 0 & d <= 104, 1.32*10^(-7)*d^4 - 2.99*10^(-5)*d^3 + 1.96*10^(-3)*d^2 - 3.02*10^(-2)*d + 0.4, 0))
}

# Bind gracefully (will return an empty tibble if neither crop exists, preventing crashes)
kc_polynomial <- dplyr::bind_rows(poly_list) 
if(base::nrow(kc_polynomial) > 0) kc_polynomial <- kc_polynomial %>% dplyr::select(-d)

# Visual Check
if(base::nrow(kc_polynomial) > 0) {
  poly_fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(kc_polynomial %>% dplyr::mutate(plot_kc = dplyr::if_else(kc == 0, NA_real_, kc)), 
         ggplot2::aes(x = doy, y = plot_kc, color = crop)) +
    ggplot2::geom_area(ggplot2::aes(fill = crop), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) + 
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(. ~ crop, ncol = 1) + 
    theme_baseR +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc")
  base::print(poly_fig)
}
```

### Grasslands and Fodder Crops

Applies calibrated drop-and-regrowth rates for grazed pastures and harvested Napier grass.

```{r kc-complex, warning=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.cap="Complex harvesting and regrowth schedules illustrating calibrated drop-and-regrowth rates for grazed pastures and Napier grass."}
no_crop <- tibble::tibble(doy = 1:366, crop = "No Crop", kc = 0)

# Safely extract grassland baseline if it exists in the user's crop list
grassland_sow <- if("Grasslands" %in% kc_wide_build$crop) kc_wide_build$Sow[kc_wide_build$crop == "Grasslands"] else NA
grassland_base <- if("Grasslands" %in% kc_segmented$crop) kc_segmented %>% dplyr::filter(crop == "Grasslands") %>% dplyr::pull(kc) else base::rep(0, 366)

# ============================================================
# GRASSLAND GROWTH CYCLE PARAMETERS 
# ============================================================

grazing_growth_rate   <- 0.00458333333333333
grazing_drop_kc       <- 0.20
grazing_max_kc        <- 0.75 
napier_decline_rate_1 <- 0.000307692307692308
napier_decline_rate_2 <- 0.000153846153846154


# 1. Define the unique variables in clean, readable lists
grazing_schedules <- list(
  "Grazed Thrice" = c(182, 243, 304),
  "Grazed 1 Aug"  = 213,
  "Grazed 1 Sept" = 244,
  "Grazed 1 Oct"  = 274,
  "Grazed 1 Nov"  = 306
)

napier_schedules <- base::list(
  "Napier"       = 1,
  "Napier Short" = 211
)

# 2. Iterate through them efficiently
complex_list <- base::list()

for (c_name in base::names(grazing_schedules)) {
  if (c_name %in% crop.param$crop) {
    complex_list[[c_name]] <- generate_grazed_legacy(c_name, grazing_schedules[[c_name]], grassland_base, grazing_growth_rate, grazing_drop_kc, grazing_max_kc, grassland_sow)
  }
}

for (c_name in base::names(napier_schedules)) {
  if (c_name %in% crop.param$crop) {
    complex_list[[c_name]] <- generate_napier(c_name, napier_schedules[[c_name]], napier_decline_rate_1, napier_decline_rate_2)
  }
}

# Bind gracefully 
complex_plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(complex_list)

# Visual Check (Only plot if there is actually complex data to show)
if (base::nrow(complex_plot_data) > 0) {
  complex_fig <- ggplot2::ggplot(complex_plot_data %>% dplyr::mutate(plot_kc = dplyr::if_else(kc == 0, NA_real_, kc)), ggplot2::aes(x = doy, y = plot_kc, color = crop)) +
    ggplot2::geom_area(ggplot2::aes(fill = crop), alpha = 0.15, show.legend = FALSE) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 1, na.rm = TRUE) + 
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ crop) + 
    theme_baseR +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Complex Harvesting & Regrowth Curves", x = "Day of Year", y = "Kc") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 366, 60), limits = c(0, 366)) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1.2, 0.3), limits = c(0, 1.2))
  base::print(complex_fig)
}
```

#### Kc Curve compilation for all crops

Compile all generated Kc curves.

```{r kc-merge}
# bind_rows handles empty dataframes perfectly, so we can safely bind everything
kc.doy.crop.all <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  kc_segmented, 
  kc_polynomial, 
  kc_fruits, 
  no_crop,
  complex_plot_data
) %>% dplyr::arrange(crop, doy)

readr::write_csv(kc.doy.crop.all, file = here::here("data/processed/supplementary/01_crop_kc_by_doy_all_crops.csv"))
```

# Cropping Systems

Read the file that describes the composition of each cropping system in terms of crop rotations at the plot scale.

```{r, load-cropping-systems}
crop.systems <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/08_crop.systems.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()

knitr::kable(crop.systems, caption = "Cropping Systems")
```

```{r, display-cropping-systems}
preview_cs <- crop.systems
cs_cols <- base::colnames(preview_cs)

# Dynamically format column names to handle varying numbers of crop_X columns
new_cols <- base::sapply(cs_cols, function(col) {
  if (col == "rotation") {
    "rotation<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Rotation ID/Code</small>"
  } else if (col == "n.rotation") {
    "n.rotation<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Rotation Year (1, 2, etc.)</small>"
  } else if (col == "crop.system") {
    "crop.system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Descriptive system name</small>"
  } else if (col == "Irrigation") {
    "Irrigation<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>System-level irrigation status</small>"
  } else if (col == "soil") {
    "soil<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Soil type code</small>"
  } else if (base::grepl("^crop_", col)) {
    base::paste0(col, "<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Internal name for a crop or Crop-Year</small>")
  } else {
    col
  }
})

base::colnames(preview_cs) <- new_cols
knitr::kable(preview_cs, escape = FALSE, caption = "Preview: Cropping Systems")
```

## Build annual/multi-annual cropping systems/rotations by compiling individual Crop Kc Curves.

```{r map-kc-curves, results='hide'}
# Generate the long-format rotation table
crop.systems.l <- crop.systems %>%
  dplyr::select(-Irrigation) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = dplyr::starts_with("crop_"), names_prefix = "crop_", names_to = "ncrop", values_to = "crop") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(crop.param, by = "crop")

crop.systems.l.kc <- crop.systems.l %>%
  dplyr::select(rotation, n.rotation, crop.system, soil, ncrop, crop, irrigation, rooting_depth_cm) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(kc.doy.crop.all %>% dplyr::arrange(doy, crop), by = "crop", relationship = "many-to-many")
```

### Daily Kc Table by Crop Rotation

*(Example showing the generated continuous timeline for a single rotation).*

```{r display-kc-expansion, echo=FALSE}
crop.rotation.kc.ls <- base::split(crop.systems.l.kc, crop.systems.l.kc$rotation)
preview_kc <- utils::head(crop.rotation.kc.ls[[1]], 10) %>%
  dplyr::select(crop.system, crop, doy, kc)

base::colnames(preview_kc) <- c(
  "crop.system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Rotation Name</small>",
  "crop<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Active Crop</small>",
  "doy<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Day of Year (1-366)</small>",
  "kc<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Daily Crop Coefficient</small>"
)

knitr::kable(preview_kc, escape = FALSE, caption = "Preview: Daily Kc Table (Single Rotation)")

readr::write_csv(crop.systems.l.kc, file = here::here("data/processed/01_crop.systems.l.kc.csv"))
```

# Production Systems

Read the file that describes the composition of each production system in terms of cropping systems and their area. For the case study in Hemingway et al. (202X), this information is taken from Tables 1 & 2 of Hemingway et al. 2025 and modified in Hemingway et al. 2026.

```{r load-production-system}
ps_by_cs_area  <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/09_crop_system_area_by_production_system.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
```

```{r display-area, echo=FALSE}
preview_ps <- ps_by_cs_area

preview_ps_disp <- preview_ps %>%
  dplyr::select(time_period, report_group_name, production_system, sub_production_system, crop.system, land_use_type, area_ha)

base::colnames(preview_ps_disp) <- c(
  "time_period<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Historical grouping</small>",
  "report_group_name<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Broader Agrarian Group</small>",
  "production_system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Agrarian Group</small>",
  "sub-production_system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Agrarian Sub-Group</small>",
  "crop.system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Implemented rotation</small>",
  "land_use_type<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Land Use Type</small>",
  "area_ha<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Cultivated area<br><b>Expected:</b> Numeric</small>"
)
knitr::kable(preview_ps_disp, escape = FALSE, caption = "Crop Area under each Production System")
```

# Agrarian System

Read the file with number of farms belonging to each of the Production Systems in the Agrarian System of the considered area (village, micro-region, watershed). In our case study these numbers are calculated for two periods using an optimisation technique as described in Hemingway et al. 2026.

```{r load-agrarian}
farms_count_df <- data.table::fread(here::here("data/input/10_no_of_farmers_by_production_system.csv")) %>% dplyr::as_tibble()
```

```{r display-counts, echo=FALSE}
preview_counts <- farms_count_df

preview_counts_disp <- preview_counts %>%
  dplyr::select(time_period, production_system, sub_production_system, number_of_farms)

base::colnames(preview_counts_disp) <- c(
  "time_period<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Historical grouping</small>",
  "production_system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Agrarian Group</small>",
  "sub_production_system<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Agrarian Sub-Group</small>",
  "number_of_farms<br><small style='color:gray; font-weight:normal;'>Total farmer count<br><b>Expected:</b> Numeric</small>"
)
knitr::kable(preview_counts_disp, escape = FALSE, caption = "Farm Counts Per Production System")
```
